verses: يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْمَلِكِ ٱلْقُدُّوسِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْحَكِيمِ
هُوَ ٱلَّذِى بَعَثَ فِى ٱلْأُمِّيِّۦنَ رَسُولًا مِّنْهُمْ يَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَإِن كَانُوا۟ مِن قَبْلُ لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
وَءَاخَرِينَ مِنْهُمْ لَمَّا يَلْحَقُوا۟ بِهِمْ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
ذَٰلِكَ فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو ٱلْفَضْلِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ

مَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ حُمِّلُوا۟ ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةَ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَحْمِلُوهَا كَمَثَلِ ٱلْحِمَارِ يَحْمِلُ أَسْفَارًۢا بِئْسَ مَثَلُ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِى ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
قُلْ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوٓا۟ إِن زَعَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ أَوْلِيَآءُ لِلَّهِ مِن دُونِ ٱلنَّاسِ فَتَمَنَّوُا۟ ٱلْمَوْتَ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
وَلَا يَتَمَنَّوْنَهُۥٓ أَبَدًۢا بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌۢ بِٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
قُلْ إِنَّ ٱلْمَوْتَ ٱلَّذِى تَفِرُّونَ مِنْهُ فَإِنَّهُۥ مُلَٰقِيكُمْ ثُمَّ تُرَدُّونَ إِلَىٰ عَٰلِمِ ٱلْغَيْبِ وَٱلشَّهَٰدَةِ فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِذَا نُودِىَ لِلصَّلَوٰةِ مِن يَوْمِ ٱلْجُمُعَةِ فَٱسْعَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ وَذَرُوا۟ ٱلْبَيْعَ ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
فَإِذَا قُضِيَتِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةُ فَٱنتَشِرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱبْتَغُوا۟ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱذْكُرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرًا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ
وَإِذَا رَأَوْا۟ تِجَٰرَةً أَوْ لَهْوًا ٱنفَضُّوٓا۟ إِلَيْهَا وَتَرَكُوكَ قَآئِمًا قُلْ مَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهْوِ وَمِنَ ٱلتِّجَٰرَةِ وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرُ ٱلرَّٰزِقِينَ

Shared motifs, rarest first: The death or fate a man flees comes after him and meets him [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in The Doomed Prince: the wife kills the snake, the dog and the crocodile pursue the prince: A crocodile in a lake and a water-being ('the Strong One') fight each other daily for months, each keeping the other in; Saved from danger, the hero offers to the sun god and praises his power every day; The fated agent itself speaks: 'I am your fate which has come after you'; 'Your god has given one of your fates into your hand': a danger overcome is credited to one's god; A wife keeps watch by her sleeping husband, makes the attacking snake drunk with beer and wine, and has it hacked to pieces; The hero refuses to have his own dog killed although it is one of his fates, because he raised it from a pup; A prince is fated to die by the crocodile, the snake or the dog.

Only in Al-Jumu'a: the messenger among the unlettered, the donkey carrying books, wishing for death, and the Friday prayer: When they saw trade or amusement they rushed to it and left the prophet standing; Those charged with the Torah who did not carry it are like a donkey carrying books (asfar); When the call to prayer is made on Friday (yawm al-jumu'a), hasten to God's remembrance and leave trading; after the prayer disperse and seek God's bounty; Challenge to the Jews: if you claim to be God's friends apart from others, wish for death, if you are truthful; they never will; The death you flee from will surely meet you; Israel likened to a donkey that knows, or does not understand, what it has [divergence between the texts]; Merchants ask when the new moon and sabbath will be over so they can sell grain with small ephah, big shekel and false scales; God raised among the unlettered (ummiyyun, Gentiles) a messenger from among them, reciting signs, purifying them and teaching the Book and wisdom; Reformer rebukes treading winepresses, loading donkeys and selling fish on the Sabbath; Trade on the weekly holy day [divergence between the texts]; The weekly holy day, and whether it rests on God's rest [divergence between the texts]; Litany of divine names: King, Holy, Peace, Faithful, Guardian, Mighty, Compeller, Proud, Creator, Maker, Fashioner; to him belong the most beautiful names; and 1 more.

matches.label: The weekly holy day, and whether it rests on God's rest
matches.note: The weekly day without the creation rest. Genesis grounds the seventh day in God's rest: wa-yišbōṯ bay-yôm haš-šəḇîʿî ... wa-yəḇāreḵ ʾĕlōhîm ʾeṯ yôm haš-šəḇîʿî wa-yqaddēš ʾōṯô kî ḇô šāḇaṯ. The Quran's Friday (yawm al-jumuʿa, the day of assembly) has no rest and no creation basis: fa-ntashirū fī l-arḍ. This fits the Quran's denial that God rested (50:38).

matches.label: Israel likened to a donkey that knows, or does not understand, what it has
matches.note: Israel compared to a donkey, in opposite directions. Isaiah: yāḏaʿ šôr qōnēhû wa-ḥămôr ʾēḇûs bəʿālâw yiśrāʾēl lōʾ yāḏaʿ (the donkey knows its master's crib, Israel does not know: the donkey is wiser). Quran: mathalu lladhīna ḥummilū t-tawrāta thumma lam yaḥmilūhā ka-mathali l-ḥimāri yaḥmilu asfārā (those charged with the Torah who did not bear it are like a donkey carrying books: the donkey carries without understanding). ḥămôr / ḥimār; in both Israel fails to 'know' what it has.

matches.label: Trade on the weekly holy day
matches.note: Trade and the weekly holy day. Nehemiah: dōrəḵîm gittôṯ baš-šabbāṯ ... û-mōḵərîm baš-šabbāṯ ... mə-ḥalləlîm ʾeṯ yôm haš-šabbāṯ, and the gates are shut from Sabbath eve to its end (wə-lōʾ yip̄tāḥûm ʿaḏ ʾaḥar haš-šabbāṯ). Quran: idhā nūdiya li-ṣ-ṣalāti min yawmi l-jumuʿati fa-sʿaw ilā dhikri llāhi wa-dharū l-bayʿ; fa-idhā quḍiyati ṣ-ṣalātu fa-ntashirū fī l-arḍi wa-btaghū min faḍli llāh. Trade stops only for the prayer, and after it the believers are told to go out and seek God's bounty (trade). A day of rest becomes an hour of assembly.

passages.text: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֡מָּה רָאִ֣יתִי בִֽיהוּדָ֣ה דֹּֽרְכִֽים גִּתּ֣וֹת בַּשַּׁבָּ֡ת וּמְבִיאִ֣ים הָעֲרֵמ֣וֹת וְֽעֹמְסִ֪ים עַל הַחֲמֹרִ֟ים וְאַף יַ֜יִן עֲנָבִ֤ים וּתְאֵנִים֙ וְכָל מַשָּׂ֔א וּמְבִיאִ֥ים יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בְּי֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֑ת וָאָעִ֕יד בְּי֖וֹם מִכְרָ֥ם צָֽיִד
וְהַצֹּרִים֙ יָ֣שְׁבוּ בָ֔הּ מְבִיאִ֥ים דָּ֖אג וְכָל מֶ֑כֶר וּמֹכְרִ֧ים בַּשַּׁבָּ֛ת לִבְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִָֽם
וָאָרִ֕יבָה אֵ֖ת חֹרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וָאֹמְרָ֣ה לָהֶ֗ם מָֽה הַדָּבָ֨ר הָרָ֤ע הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם עֹשִׂ֔ים וּֽמְחַלְּלִ֖ים אֶת י֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּֽת

passages.text: (13:15) בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֡מָּה רָאִ֣יתִי בִֽיהוּדָ֣ה דֹּֽרְכִֽים גִּתּ֣וֹת בַּשַּׁבָּ֡ת וּמְבִיאִ֣ים הָעֲרֵמ֣וֹת וְֽעֹמְסִ֪ים עַל הַחֲמֹרִ֟ים וְאַף יַ֜יִן עֲנָבִ֤ים וּתְאֵנִים֙ וְכָל מַשָּׂ֔א וּמְבִיאִ֥ים יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בְּי֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֑ת וָאָעִ֕יד בְּי֖וֹם מִכְרָ֥ם צָֽיִד (13:16) וְהַצֹּרִים֙ יָ֣שְׁבוּ בָ֔הּ מְבִיאִ֥ים דָּ֖אג וְכָל מֶ֑כֶר וּמֹכְרִ֧ים בַּשַּׁבָּ֛ת לִבְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִָֽם (13:17) וָאָרִ֕יבָה אֵ֖ת חֹרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וָאֹמְרָ֣ה לָהֶ֗ם מָֽה הַדָּבָ֨ר הָרָ֤ע הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם עֹשִׂ֔ים וּֽמְחַלְּלִ֖ים אֶת י֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּֽת (13:18) הֲל֨וֹא כֹ֤ה עָשׂוּ֙ אֲבֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וַיָּבֵ֨א אֱלֹהֵ֜ינוּ עָלֵ֗ינוּ אֵ֚ת כָּל הָרָעָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את וְעַ֖ל הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֑את וְאַתֶּ֞ם מוֹסִיפִ֤ים חָרוֹן֙ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְחַלֵּ֖ל אֶת הַשַּׁבָּֽת
